deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing pp. 30–32): X is a stratified space, here just X = X* ⊔ Y with Y a closed stratum. V_{Y,X} is a tubular neighbourhood germ of Y in X and V*_{Y,X} = V_{Y,X} \ Y is the deleted (punctured) tubular neighbourhood. The previous page gave a van Kampen pushout, eq. (9): π1(X) ≅ π1(X*) *_{π1 V*_{Y,X}} π1(V_{Y,X}), with π1(V_{Y,X}) ≅ π1(Y). To make π1(X) explicit from 'elementary' data, one must understand π1(V*_{Y,X}) and its two maps, diagram (10).

This page says this is where the hypothesis of normal local triviality matters. Its earlier role (in Esquisse-style tame topology) was 'rather heuristic'. What one really has to prove is that the homotopy properties of the inclusion V*_{Y,X} ↪ V_{Y,X} are those of a locally trivial fibration. Here V_{Y,X} is identified with Y by a 'homotopism', i.e. a deformation retraction, marginal note. The fibre is the punctured normal slice V*_{z,Z}, where z ∈ Y and Z is a germ of normal (transversal) slice at z.

This is statement (11): V*_{Y,X} → V_{Y,X} ≃ Y is a homotopy fibration with fibre the punctured normal-slice germ (the link of Y). Grothendieck then proposes to take (11) as the DEFINITION of 'homotopical local triviality' of Y ↪ X in topos-theoretic contexts, e.g. schemes with the étale topology. There one must use profinite homotopy types, localized at the primes different from the residual characteristics, as in Artin–Mazur, since only there do finiteness theorems hold (continued on the next page).

The next page draws the long exact sequence (12)/(13). When the link is connected, π1(V*_{Y,X}) is an extension of π1(Y) by a quotient of π1 of the link. This is a stratified dévissage of π1 via van Kampen plus a link fibration.
errors: Notational inconsistency in the fibre. Line 7 has V*_{z,Z} (point z, normal slice Z), while in (11) it is written V*_{z,X}. The fibre of the punctured tubular neighbourhood over Y must be the punctured normal slice / link, V*_{z,Z}, not the punctured neighbourhood of z in X. That neighbourhood includes the directions along Y and is contractible-up-to-link-suspension rather than the link itself. So 'X' in (11) is a slip.

The fibration claim is only heuristic or definitional here. In topology it requires a hypothesis such as Whitney/Thom–Mather conditions or Quinn's homotopical stratification. In the étale setting it fails without restricting to primes ≠ residual characteristics (wild ramification), as Grothendieck himself flags.

ideas.what: Van Kampen dévissage of π1 of a stratified space along a closed stratum via the deleted tubular neighbourhood, needing π1 of the link fibration
ideas.modern_name: stratified van Kampen / dévissage of fundamental groups; exit-path and link methods
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (van Kampen); stratified versions: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures), in outline

ideas.what: Replace geometric normal local triviality by the purely homotopical condition that the punctured tubular neighbourhood → stratum is a homotopy fibration with fibre the link
ideas.modern_name: homotopically stratified spaces (holink evaluation is a fibration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: F. Quinn, 'Homotopically stratified sets' (JAMS 1988); B. Hughes

ideas.what: Use this homotopy-fibration property as the definition of local triviality along a stratum in étale/topos contexts, with profinite homotopy types localized away from residue characteristics
ideas.modern_name: étale homotopy links / étale tubular neighbourhoods; stratified étale homotopy (exodromy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Mazur (1969); D. Cox, étale tubular neighbourhoods (1979); Grothendieck–Murre tame π1 of formal neighbourhoods (1971); Barwick–Glasman–Haine exodromy, Haine on étale links (2018–)
ideas.where_published: related tame π1 material in SGA1 XIII and Grothendieck–Murre (LNM 208); the definitional proposal is not known to me in print

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes, in a topos/étale setting, an axiomatic notion of 'homotopical local triviality' of a stratification Y ⊂ X. The punctured étale tubular neighbourhood should be a (prime-to-residue-characteristic, profinite) homotopy fibration over Y with fibre the punctured normal slice. He intends it as the working hypothesis for dévissage of étale π1 and higher homotopy (exact sequences (12)/(13)).
missed.quote: c'est cela qui devrait même, dans le contexte topossique (p. ex. celui des schémas avec la top. étale) servir comme de définition de la "locale trivialité homotopique" de l'inclusion Y ↪ X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The topological analogue was formalized independently by Quinn (1988). The étale analogue is close to current work on étale homotopy links and exodromy (Barwick–Glasman–Haine, Haine). There, a condition 'link map is a fibration away from p' singles out tamely/locally-acyclically stratified schemes. Grothendieck's proposal anticipates using this as a definition, linked to a van Kampen dévissage of π1, which is not standard in the literature as a named notion.

deep.surprise_reason: The idea is a clear, early (c. 1981) formulation of 'homotopical local triviality' as the fibration property of the deleted tubular neighbourhood. It predates Quinn's homotopically stratified sets and is transplanted to étale topoi with profinite, prime-to-p localization. It is natural for experts and partly anticipated by Cox's and Artin–Mazur's work, so it is only mildly surprising.
transcription_corrections: Equation label '(II)' should be '(11)', consistent with (9),(10) on the previous page and (12),(13) on the next.
The fibre at line 7 reads V*_{z,Z} (lowercase z, a point of Y; Z a normal slice), not V*_{Z,Z}. In (11) the manuscript reads V*_{z,X}, apparently a slip for V*_{z,Z}.
The marginal annotation reads 'homotopisme' with a vertical arrow V_{Y,X} ↕ Y, i.e. the retraction V_{Y,X} → Y is a homotopy equivalence.
'sans dessus' is crossed out; the inserted word is 'types' (types d'homotopie profinis).
'listés [?] vestiaux' is unclear in the image. The parenthetical seems to dismiss some (verticality/local-triviality) condition as 'techniquement inutile'; read with caution.
'servir comme de définition': 'comme' is an insertion above the line.
